question: Are the 18.8% of generated molecules that RDKit ETKDG cannot embed a VELOCITY-STAGE failure? A coordinate-space guidance term (the whole BLK-C-L3 family: EnFlow arXiv:2512.22597, PCFM ICLR 2026, FlowBack-Adjoint arXiv:2508.03619) can only help if the sampled COORDINATES are the defective object.

cohort.provenance: free generation via the ODE (cfm_free_generation_panel_seed0.json), checkpoint cfm_fullcorpus_2026_10_10 epoch 10

protocol: ETKDGv3, useRandomCoords=True, maxAttempts=1, randomSeed=0xF00D -- the definition in molmetal/scripts/wf_blkc4_metric_validity_audit.py::embeddable, which reproduces the audit's recorded 54/66 = 0.8182 exactly.

THE_DECISIVE_TEST.question: Does EmbedMolecule read the model's coordinates, or only the molecular graph?
THE_DECISIVE_TEST.method: Attach a deliberately absurd conformer (atom i placed at (999i, -999i, 0.5i)) to every molecule, then call EmbedMolecule with clearConfs=True. If ETKDG used the input coordinates, the garbage conformer would change the outcome.
THE_DECISIVE_TEST.result: 11/66 fail with the garbage conformer present; 11/66 fail without it. IDENTICAL.
THE_DECISIVE_TEST.conclusion: MEASURED. RDKit's EmbedMolecule builds a conformer from the molecular graph and never reads the model's coordinates. The model's 3D output is DISCARDED by this metric.
THE_DECISIVE_TEST.why_this_is_the_load_bearing_fact: It means the 18.8% embed-failure rate is a property of the decoded MOLECULAR GRAPH -- the bond head's output -- not of the velocity field's geometry. A force injected into the coordinate trajectory cannot change a number that never looks at the trajectory.

localisation_of_the_failure.method: Delete every metal atom (Z in {Pt,Ru,Ir,Rh,Os,Re}) from each failing molecule and re-run the identical embed protocol.
localisation_of_the_failure.result: 11 of the 12 failing molecules become embeddable once the metal is removed.
localisation_of_the_failure.conclusion: MEASURED. The failure is localised at the METAL COORDINATION CENTRE, not in the organic skeleton. Ring strain is not the driver: 3 of the 11 failures contain NO rings at all (minring=0), so ring geometry cannot be the common cause.
localisation_of_the_failure.supporting_measurement: metal_max_degree is NOT the discriminator: mean 4.87 in the 55 that embed vs 4.91 in the 11 that fail, and both cohorts are full of degree-6 centres (23 generated molecules have a degree-6 metal and 22 of them embed fine). So it is not simply 'too many bonds to the metal'.
localisation_of_the_failure.why_this_matches_a_known_RDKit_limitatio: molmetal/scripts/check_3d_embed.py:156-160 already records it: 'RDKit has no ETKDG torsion parameters for transition metals (Pt, Ru, Ir), so the knowledge-term distance geometry fails.' The 12 failures are RDKit's metal-blindness, not malformed chemistry.

denominator_reconciliation.resolution: MEASURED, both are correct over their own denominator: restricting the same 66 rows to n_fragments==1 gives exactly 52/64 = 0.8125. Same 54 successes, two denominators. This is NOT a discrepancy; the two documents simply never said which denominator they used.
denominator_reconciliation.recommended_citation: state the denominator inline every time

the_second_unreproducible_number.claim_in_the_audit_report: 'chemistry_validity_pass_rate 66/66 = 1.0000 generated, 635/636 = 0.9984 real, reproducing the recorded panel exactly.'
the_second_unreproducible_number.problem: Neither string appears anywhere in metrics/by_metric/cfm_metric_validity_audit.json. The claim was TRUE but not ON DISK, which is this project's own rule (AGENTS.md 1).
the_second_unreproducible_number.resolution_2026_10_12: Re-measured independently against molmetal/scripts/cfm_property_panel.py::_validate_molecule: generated 66/66, reconstructed 635/636. Both reproduce exactly. The numbers are now sourced to a named function.

what_this_does_NOT_show: It does NOT say the generated molecules are chemically fine. A graph that RDKit cannot embed is still a graph the downstream docking and property pipelines cannot use.

It does NOT clear the bond head. The 11/12 metal-removal result says the BOND HEAD is emitting metal coordination spheres that no conformer generator accepts -- which is a bond-head defect, and it is squarely on the macro-F1(TYPE) axis this line already loses.

verdict.L5_cause_localised_to: the bond head's metal coordination output (graph-level), not the velocity field (coordinate-level)
verdict.reasoning: Every method in the cited guidance family acts on coordinates. The failure metric discards coordinates (MEASURED above). Injecting a force cannot change a graph, and the failure is in the graph.
verdict.what_L3_guidance_would_actually_act_on: if a guidance term were built, its only path to the reported failures would be INDIRECT -- better coordinates feeding a better bond head. That is a real but unmeasured and indirect coupling, and it is not what the cited papers claim.
